competitive_landscape: A dense inter-island ferry network (Native Son, Road Town Fast Ferry, Smith's, Speedy's) plus the world's largest bareboat-charter fleet move people today — overwhelming demand proof and the obvious partners. The pain is slow displacement hulls, customs friction, and fragmented private transfers; there is no foiling incumbent.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: This is the strongest Pioneer II node in the hemisphere — virtually the entire USVI-BVI archipelago (St Thomas/St John/Tortola/Jost Van Dyke/Virgin Gorda/St Croix) sits inside 40 nm, so the all-electric platform owns the whole daily network.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) adds the only long leg that matters — the ~80-nm Anegada Passage to St-Maarten/Anguilla — connecting the Virgins to the northern Leewards.

precedents.what: The Bali→Lombok→Komodo and Maldives island-hopping chains
precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrate the dense-archipelago premium-transfer model the Virgins mirror — at even tighter ranges.

regulatory_note: Dual-jurisdiction: USCG (Subchapter T) on the US side and the UK Red Ensign / BVI Shipping Registry on the UK side, with customs/immigration at each crossing. A scheduled premium operator that streamlines clearance is itself a differentiator. Virgin Islands National Park favors zero-emission, low-wake vessels.
seasonality: Atlantic hurricane season (Jun–Nov, peak Sep) is the main constraint; charter high season is Dec–Apr. The Sir Francis Drake Channel and Pillsbury Sound are relatively protected, supporting a long shoulder season for Pioneer II.
summary: The US and British Virgin Islands pack dozens of inhabited islands and anchorages into a ~30-nm box: St Thomas, St John, Water Island and St Croix (US), and Tortola, Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke and Anegada (UK). Almost every leg sits comfortably inside Pioneer II range, and the daily reality is a constant churn of inter-island ferries plus a tedious US/UK customs dance at Cruz Bay, Red Hook, Road Town and West End. This is the global charter capital (The Moorings, Sunsail, Dream Yacht all base here), making it the densest luxury-charter and tourism cluster in the hemisphere.
tagline: The tightest island cluster on earth for an all-electric foiler — and the charter capital of the world.
